title: Obedience (I.9)
hook: being in charge looks like freedom; chapter nine says it's safer to be under direction, and safer to hear advice than give it
tomorrow: if you fixed just one fault a year, where would you start?

segments.voice: Yesterday, two printouts at a lectern and chapter five's answer: mark what is said, not who said it, or how grandly. The line was truth, not style.

Being the one in charge looks like freedom. You pick the plan. Nobody tells you no. Chapter nine of The Imitation of Christ looks at that picture and turns it around. It's much safer, it says, to stand under obedience than to be in charge. And safer to hear advice than to give it. Safer. Why would that be?
screen: `IN CHARGE LOOKS LIKE FREEDOM.` → `SAFER UNDER OBEDIENCE.` → `SAFER TO HEAR THAN TO GIVE.`

segments.voice: The chapter was written for a religious community, where obedience to a superior is a promise. It's honest about how that goes: some obey out of necessity, not love, and grumble. But its reason reaches anyone. Everyone likes their own opinion, it says, and leans toward people who agree. Who is so wise as to know everything? So don't trust your own view too much; be willing to hear others. Even when your view is good, letting it go for peace, for God's sake, is wiser than digging in. That's why direction is safer: the person under it has another pair of eyes. Here's a neighbor who says something close. In the Dhammapada, a collection of the Buddha's sayings, one verse says, put simply: if you find a wise person who points out your faults, as someone would point out hidden treasure, follow that person; it will go better for you, not worse. That's the thing to tell a friend tonight: two old traditions both call correction from someone wiser a treasure, not a loss. And the honest difference. For the Imitation, obedience is for the love of God, in a community where God is among them. The Dhammapada isn't speaking of obeying God; it points to a wise guide on the path the Buddha taught.
screen: `SOME OBEY, AND GRUMBLE.` · `WHO KNOWS EVERYTHING?` · `THE DHAMMAPADA: FAULTS AS TREASURE.` · `FOR GOD'S SAKE, OR ON THE PATH.` · then, large: `UNDER DIRECTION.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers three pieces of advice you once resisted that turned out right, and give each person a moment of thanks. Then let one more come to mind, advice you're resisting now, and hold it as if it might be treasure.
Obedience. In chapter nine, living under direction and hearing counsel, safer than ruling by your own opinion.
Your line: under direction. Another pair of eyes is a gift, even when it stings a little. Good night.

howItsDone: Catholic religious make a vow of obedience to their superiors, and lay Catholics may seek a spiritual director or a trusted confessor whose counsel they weigh and follow.

chat.says: dad says sit out friday to rest my ankle. abuela: "el que no oye consejo..." ugh. do i listen?
options: Weigh it honestly, then probably yes. Chapter nine says hearing counsel is safer than giving it.
Only if he's right about everything. Otherwise trust yourself; you know your body best.
Always, about anything, no questions asked. Obedience means you don't get to think.
chat.meaning: Chapter nine: don't trust your own opinion too much; it's safer to hear and take counsel than to give it. Abuela's proverb agrees.

Dhammapada.meaning: a collection of the Buddha's sayings in verse

the Buddha.meaning: the teacher whose path Buddhists follow

superior.meaning: the leader of a religious community

The Imitation of Christ.meaning: a short book of counsel credited to Thomas à Kempis

sources.work: The Imitation of Christ (attributed to Thomas à Kempis)

notes: Imitation I.9 paraphrased: a great thing to stand in obedience, live under a superior, and not be one's own master; much safer to be in subjection than in authority; many are under obedience more from necessity than love, and grumble; everyone is inclined to his own opinion and to those who agree; who is so wise as to know all things?; do not trust your own opinion too much, but be willing to hear others; even if your opinion is good, to give it up for God is more profitable; it is safer to hear and take counsel than to give it. Confirm.

v3 unity thread (wisdom day): Dhammapada 76 paraphrased (Max Müller 1881 is public domain, but the exact wording was not verified, so it is not quoted): one who shows your faults is like one who reveals hidden treasure; follow such a wise person; it will be better, not worse. Shared: correction from someone wiser as treasure. Difference: obedience for God's sake in a community vs following a wise guide on the Buddha's path, with no talk of obeying God. Confirm a Buddhist reader would find this fair.
